description: GOBACK RETURNING/GIVING identifier — an IMPLEMENTOR EXTENSION, not an ISO phrase (kb/Work PB407). §2023:14.9.18.2's general format has exactly two alternatives inside its choice-indicator bracket, raising-phrase and status-phrase; there is no RETURNING or GIVING phrase, and §2023:14.9.18.4 GR2's RETURNING is the PROCEDURE DIVISION HEADER's item, not a phrase of the statement. The row is kept because the extension is accepted (the shipped 2002/goback_returning.cob golden runs it) and is gated at 2002 because GOBACK itself is a 2002 introduction — but it no longer cites a GOBACK clause as the authority for a phrase that clause does not contain. The 2002 edge is GOBACK's own. THE EDGE IS QUOTED from the edition texts (kb/Work PB3965): COBOL-85 ends a run unit with STOP RUN, 'If the RUN phrase is specified, execution of the run unit ceases and control is transferred to the operating system.' (§1985:VI.6.24.4 GR1), and a called program with EXIT PROGRAM, 'The EXIT PROGRAM statement marks the logical end of a called program.' (§1985:X.5.4.1), and has no GOBACK; 2002 adds 'The GOBACK statement marks the logical end of a function, a method, or a program.' (§2002:14.8.17), §2002:F.1 item 6 lists GOBACK under 'Reserved words. The following reserved words have been added', and §2002:F.2 states the change, its item 62: 'GOBACK statement. A GOBACK statement has been added that always returns control, either to the operating system or to the calling runtime element.' §2014:14.9.17 and §2023:14.9.18.1 carry the 2002 sentence. The 2002 general format (§2002:14.8.17.1) is GOBACK with an optional RAISING phrase only, no RETURNING or GIVING phrase either; 'The GOBACK statement shall not be specified in a declarative procedure' is its one syntax rule (§2002:14.8.17.2 SR1).
vcr: 2002 introduction of GOBACK (§2002:F.2 item 62); RETURNING/GIVING is an implementor extension (kb/Work PB407)
